column3: USDA general below-fiber-saturation moist wood heat-capacity model
column4: Source population, moisture convention and scope
column5: General wood engineering correlation from Chapter 4, not a measured species, product or specimen card. The handbook describes specific heat as practically independent of density and species; no species qualification or source pressure is supplied. Moisture content is x=100*m_water/m_oven_dry_wood (Equations 4-1 and 4-2); the admitted moisture axis is the dimensionless dry-basis mass ratio m=x/100, not wet-mass fraction or relative humidity. The source states validity below fiber saturation from 280 to 420 K. Fiber saturation varies with species and specimen; no universal 30 percent boundary is inferred. A fixed-moisture sensible-capacity interpretation is explicit; there is no drying, moisture transport, latent heat, sorption transfer, density or species-specific thermal law. Capacity is per kilogram of total moist wood (wood plus retained water), not per kilogram of dry wood. A body with dry mass M_d requires the supplied fixed moist mass M_d*(1+m). The 0 to 20 percent dry-basis moisture interval is an authored subset; the separate below-fiber-saturation condition is still mandatory.

column3: USDA general below-fiber-saturation moist wood heat-capacity model
column5: c_p,x=(c_p0+4.18*x/100)/(1+x/100)+A_c; c_p0=0.1031+0.003867*T; A_c=x*(-0.06191+0.000236*T-0.000133*x). T is kelvin, x is dry-basis moisture percent and c_p,x is kJ/(kg of total moist wood K). Stored values multiply by 1000 for J/(kg K) and substitute x=100*m. A_c is the source fixed-moisture wood-water bond adjustment, not an independently available heat-of-sorption or continuous-drying law. Source uncertainty is unstated.

column5: 328 values use 70-digit decimal arithmetic at T=280,300,...,420 K and m=0,0.005,...,0.20. The 560 explicitly authored triangles split each rectangle from its high-temperature/low-moisture corner to its low-temperature/high-moisture corner. The handbook does not publish this mesh. Linear surface interpolation approximates the source equation between nodes. Checks at each triangle centroid, three quarter/quarter/half barycentric points and three edge midpoints have maximum observed relative difference 0.042192307526564863 percent, below 0.06 percent. This finite comparison is not a continuous certified error bound or a source uncertainty estimate. The nodes are model evaluations, not independent experiments; fixed moisture on a stored moisture row reproduces the affine temperature equation.
